cases.result: The application reads the authenticated session.

operation.auth.list-sessions.reason: Session ownership is checked in isolated Worker/D1 tests. WebKit journeys verify browser mutations and reload persistence, including injected service failures followed by real Worker retries. Service workers are blocked in these auth journeys; development service-worker reload verification remains separate.
audience: Authenticated session owner; anonymous callers refused

cases.test: revoking other sessions preserves the current session and other users
cases.result: The caller sees only their sessions; after revoking others the list contains exactly the current session.

cases.test: anonymous callers cannot list or revoke sessions
cases.result: Anonymous requests receive 401 and do not revoke the existing session.

cases.test: revoking a device through the browser persists after both devices reload
cases.result: The selected device loses its session after reload while the current device stays signed in.

cases.test: revoking all other devices preserves this browser and an unrelated account after reload
cases.result: Only the current session remains after reload; another account stays signed in.

operation.auth.revoke-other-sessions.reason: Session ownership is checked in isolated Worker/D1 tests. WebKit journeys verify browser mutations and reload persistence, including injected service failures followed by real Worker retries. Service workers are blocked in these auth journeys; development service-worker reload verification remains separate.
audience: Authenticated session owner; anonymous callers refused

cases.test: revoking other sessions preserves the current session and other users
cases.result: Other sessions for this account lose authentication while the current session and another user remain signed in.

cases.test: anonymous callers cannot list or revoke sessions
cases.result: Anonymous requests receive 401 and do not revoke the existing session.

cases.test: revoking all other devices preserves this browser and an unrelated account after reload
cases.result: Only the current session remains after reload; another account stays signed in.

cases.test: failed revoke-all keeps other sessions and retries successfully against the Worker
cases.result: A simulated 503 leaves the other session signed in; retry reaches the real Worker and the other browser is signed out after reload.

operation.auth.revoke-session.reason: Session ownership is checked in isolated Worker/D1 tests. WebKit journeys verify browser mutations and reload persistence, including injected service failures followed by real Worker retries. Service workers are blocked in these auth journeys; development service-worker reload verification remains separate.
audience: Authenticated session owner; anonymous callers refused

cases.test: revoking one owned session ends that session and preserves the caller
cases.result: The revoked cookie loses authentication and the session disappears from the list; the caller remains signed in.

cases.test: anonymous callers cannot list or revoke sessions
cases.result: Anonymous requests receive 401 and do not revoke the existing session.

cases.test: knowing another user session token does not authorize revoking it
cases.result: A token belonging to another user survives a revocation attempt by the caller.

cases.test: revoking a device through the browser persists after both devices reload
cases.result: The selected device loses its session after reload while the current device stays signed in.

cases.test: failed device revocation keeps the session and retries successfully against the Worker
cases.result: A simulated 503 preserves the session and enables retry; the retry revokes it through the real Worker and survives reload.
